title: Interpretation
description: A reading of evidence that a reasonable analyst could dispute (CONSTITUTION §3). NOT a claim — it has no source of its own. NOT an opinion — it has explicit reasoning and a stated falsification test. This record type exists because the Atlas kept producing structurally-sound arguments it had nowhere to put, and the alternative was either discarding them or laundering them into findings.

statement.description: The interpretation, stated so it could be wrong. Hedged phrasing that cannot be falsified is not an interpretation, it is a mood.

reasoning.description: The argument, step by step. Each step must be independently checkable. An interpretation whose reasoning cannot be written out is an opinion and belongs in a different field.

rests_on.description: Claim IDs the reasoning depends on. May be empty ONLY when the argument is purely structural (arithmetic, definitional). Structural arguments must say so in reasoning.

falsified_by.description: MANDATORY. What observation would show this is wrong. An interpretation with no falsification condition cannot be published — that is the line between interpretation and opinion.

status.description: 'unfalsified' is the honest default and means only that nobody has checked. 'untestable' requires a recorded reason and downgrades the record to opinion.

strength.description: structural = follows from arithmetic or definition; strong = multiple independent lines converge; plausible = one line of reasoning; speculative = a hunch with a shape.

scope.description: Who this applies to. An interpretation that silently generalizes is the failure mode this whole record type exists to prevent.

competing.description: Other interpretation IDs that would explain the same evidence differently. Recording the competitor is what stops an interpretation hardening into a belief.

render.description: Locked. The interface MUST render this visually distinct from facts and must never let it enter a recommendation unlabelled (CONSTITUTION §3).
